newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oil imports seen up 22 pct in 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oil imports seen up 22 pct in 1996 - paper.

text.p: Oil and lubricants imports by Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras are expected to grow 22 percent to $6.3 billion this year, compared with $5.18 billion in 1995, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil, quoting Petrobras officials, said the expected hike in imports was due mostly to a jump in domestic consumer demand for oil derivatives and higher world prices.
A rise in oil imports was behind a jump in Brazil's monthly trade deficit in September.
The newspaper said oil and derivatives imports reached $4.27 billion in the January-September period, totalling $665 million in September alone or 70 percent higher than the same month last year.
Petrobras's trade director, Percy Louzada de Abreu, said average daily purchases this year should reach the equivalent of 800,000 barrels per day (bpd), according to Gazeta.
